issues.description: Getter name for StockIngredient differs between template and solution. Template repository defines StockIngredient#getIngredientName() while the solution repository defines StockIngredient#getName(). Corresponding uses in Stock.findStockIngredient in each repo call the matching getter, but the mismatch across artifacts can confuse students (the problem statement asks to "add getters for all the private fields" without prescribing names) and may lead to inconsistencies when comparing template, solution, and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick a single getter name for the StockIngredient name field and use it consistently across template, solution, and any tests. Recommended: use getName() (update template StockIngredient to provide getName() and update Stock.findStockIngredient to call getName()), or alternatively change the solution to getIngredientName(). Also update the problem statement to explicitly state the expected getter names to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: Inconsistent getter name for the ingredient's name field across artifacts. The problem statement (asks to “add getters for all the private fields” but does not prescribe names) refers to adding getters in general. In the template repository, StockIngredient defines the getter as getIngredientName() and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls x.getIngredientName(); in the solution repository, StockIngredient defines the getter as getName() and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls x.getName(). Because the same conceptual property (the StockIngredient name) is exposed with two different method names (getIngredientName vs getName), students may implement one form while tests or other code expect the other, causing confusion or failing builds/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter for the ingredient name consistent across template, solution, and tests. Prefer the conventional name getName(): rename the template's StockIngredient.getIngredientName() to getName(), update all references in template Stock.findStockIngredient() to call getName(), and ensure tests/reference code use getName(). Alternatively, if changing the solution is preferred, rename the solution getter to getIngredientName() and update references there — but ensure all occurrences across code and tests use the same identifier.
